title: Pin-change eval orchestrator with priority profiles and cost thresholds
creator: Priya Singh
description: Build an orchestrator service that automatically schedules and executes targeted eval runs when a model version is pinned or upgraded (catalog or customer-pinned). The orchestrator will apply priority profiles (e.g., production-critical customers vs. low-impact) and cost thresholds to determine sampling strategy, evaluation suites, and whether to run smoke/synthetic checks, full regression suites, or a staged canary evaluation. The goal is fast, actionable quality signals on pin events while bounding run cost and avoiding noisy false positives for low-risk changes.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator triggers on both catalog updates and customer pin events within 60s of the event
Priority profiles can be defined per-customer and per-catalog-entry and honored by the scheduler
Cost threshold config prevents full regression runs unless estimated token cost is below configured limit
Evaluation results are written to the evals store and surfaced in Console with a dedicated "Pin Change Evaluations" dashboard
Automatic notification rules created: blocking alerts for high-severity regressions and informational for low-severity diffs
Backfill mode supports re-running the same policy for historical pin events via a CLI command
updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff with Eng (Miguel, Tara) and Research (Evan). Agreed to reuse existing eval runners and add an orchestration layer instead of modifying runner internals.
2026-02-28: Wireframe for Console UI created (Drive: https://drive.google.com/rd/pin-evals-wireframe). UX requested a compact summary card + link to full diff and per-metric trendlines.
2026-03-03: Engineering spike completed: prototype webhook adapter for pin events (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2345). Latency measured at ~150ms end-to-end in dev cluster.
2026-03-06: Decision to implement priority profiles: profiles = [critical, standard, experimental]. Each profile maps to sample size, eval suites, and cost cap.
2026-03-09: Trade-off discussion: sampling fewer examples reduces cost but increases variance. Agreed to implement progressive sampling—start small, expand on borderline diffs.
2026-03-12: Validation tests for cost estimator added to CI (ENG PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2401).
decisions: Adopt orchestrator pattern (stateless scheduler + durable job-store) to allow retries and cross-region coordination
Use existing eval suites (smoke, targeted, full-regression) but allow ad-hoc bundles for customer-specific tests
Implement cost estimator using token distribution histograms collected from realtime logs rather than per-request tracing to keep overhead low
Expose knobs in Console: override profile for single pin, force full regression (with approval), and opt-out for low-risk customers
risks: False positives from small-sample evals could trigger unnecessary rollbacks—mitigated by progressive sampling and confidence thresholds
Large customers with extensive prompt sets may exceed cost caps and block full regressions—mitigated via customer-specific profiles and manual approval flow
Orchestrator mis-scheduling could create load spikes on eval infra—mitigated by rate limits and prioritization windows
Data residency constraints for private deployments require the orchestration runner to be configurable to run in-customer VPCs (further engineering work required)
next_steps: Complete orchestrator MVP: job store, scheduler, webhook adapter, and basic Console surface (2 weeks)
Add progressive sampling logic and confidence thresholding into eval runner (Eng + Research collaboration)
Create default priority profiles and expose JSON schema in Console for customer overrides
Schedule a stakeholder demo and failover tabletop for SRE and Customer Success teams
